summary: Economics and data science, with monetary policy as the throughline: coursework, a co-authored paper, and founding the college's Fed Challenge team.
context: Davidson is a liberal arts college, and the economics work here was deliberately paired with that: the argument of the Fed Challenge team was that an economics education is stronger read through a liberal arts perspective, not narrower.
actions: Co-authored a paper on adapting rules-based monetary policy to crisis intervention for ECO 495, What's Wrong With Economics?, under Dr. Jaya Jha.
Founded and organized the college's first Fed Challenge team as an independent study with Prof. Caleb Stroup.
Served as a macroeconomics teaching assistant.

outcomes.claim: Co-authored a paper on the Federal Reserve's COVID-19 response, concluding with a three-pronged crisis playbook: deliver liquidity quickly, coordinate with fiscal policy, and tie every intervention to transparent, data-linked exit criteria.
Graduated with a BA in Economics and Data Science.

evidence.title: Challenges of Adapting a Rules Based Monetary Policy Approach to Crisis Intervention
evidence.note: With Zuber Chawla. ECO 495, Dr. Jaya Jha, May 2025. Hosted here. Open it.

summary: Co-initiated Davidson's first Fed Challenge team as a student-led independent study; it placed in the top 15% nationally and became a permanent economics course.
context: The College Fed Challenge is a national competition in which undergraduate teams simulate an FOMC meeting: analyzing conditions, forecasting, identifying risks and recommending policy. Davidson had never entered. There was no team, no syllabus and no precedent.
actions: Initiated the team as a student-led independent study with Will Bacdayan and Bilal Razzak, under Prof. Caleb Stroup.
Wrote a syllabus and recruited a team to represent Davidson for the first time.
Sought out resources from economics faculty and students across the college.
Presented on monetary policy to residents of the Town of Davidson.

outcomes.claim: The inaugural team placed in the top 15% of 120 participating institutions.
Prof. Stroup formalized the effort as ECO 386, a permanent economics department course, so it outlived the team that started it.
The program went on to reach the 2026 national finals, finishing among the top six nationally against Harvard, UCLA, Penn and Chicago.
I was invited to dine with Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson during his visit to Davidson, at the president’s house.

evidence.title: Davidson College: Davidson's Fed Challenge team reaches national finals
evidence.note: Names the 2024 founding team and records both the top-15% debut and the 2026 finals run.
